meta.title: PARENT ABSENCE NOTIFICATION
meta.subtitle: Software Design Document (SDD)
meta.tagline: Enhancement of the SAMS Attendance Module
meta.guideline: Prepared in alignment with the Phase-2 (Software Design) guideline
meta.status: Completed Design Baseline - Pending Stakeholder Approval

blocks.text: **Executive assessment:** The Release 1 design covers every Must and Should requirement in the BRD (BR-01 to BR-11) and is traceable to tests. Production approval should depend on cleaning up missing student–parent links, confirming SendGrid sending limits, and naming an owner for the 11:00 follow-up list. **Decision requested:** approve F-01 to F-08 for implementation, subject to the release gates in Section 12.3. The main delivery risks are incomplete guardian data, email deliverability at the 08:30 peak, and correct handling of corrections made shortly after cut-off.

This document describes the software design for adding parent absence notifications to the existing SAMS attendance module. It combines architectural and detailed design so the enhancement can be reviewed before implementation and maintained after release.

rows: First complete design baseline produced from BRD v1.0 (20 October 2026).

blocks.text: The BRD leaves several design choices open. To make this SDD implementation-ready without presenting those choices as decided facts, this version adopts the following explicit baseline. Any later change must be recorded as a versioned design change before production release.

items: Release 1 includes features F-01 to F-08 defined in Section 4. SMS and Telegram remain out of scope (BRD §6).
Notification processing runs as a scheduled job every minute; the first absence run for a school is at its configured cut-off time (default 08:30, school time zone Asia/Phnom_Penh).
A correction window of 30 minutes after a notification is sent applies; changing Absent to Present within this window sends one correction message.
Release 1 channels are email (SendGrid) and in-app (parent portal). Each parent must keep at least one channel enabled.
Absence-reason links are signed, single-student tokens valid for 72 hours; parents who are logged in can also answer from the portal.
Attachments for absence reasons are limited to PDF, JPG and PNG up to 5 MB each.
Notification logs and absence reasons are kept for the current academic year plus 90 days, then deleted; monthly aggregates are kept for 3 years.
Templates are stored per event type and language (English, Khmer); the parent's preferred language decides which is used, with English as fallback.

blocks.text: The purpose of this design is to notify parents promptly when a student is absent or late, let them submit a reason, and give staff a reliable record, without changing how teachers take attendance. It defines the interface, components, data flows, database changes, APIs, security controls and tests needed.

items: Automatic absence and late notifications after a configurable cut-off time.
Correction messages when attendance is changed to Present within the correction window.
Email and in-app channels, with parent channel preferences.
Parent absence-reason submission with optional attachment.
Staff view of reasons and an office follow-up list.
Administrator configuration of cut-off times, late notifications and bilingual templates.
Notification log and monthly absence/notification report.
SMS, Telegram or other messaging channels (phase 2).
Automatic absence prediction or risk scoring.
Changes to the teacher attendance-taking screens or QR check-in flow.
Fixing guardian data in source systems beyond the data-quality report in Section 12.

blocks.text: SAMS already records daily attendance through the web screen and QR-code check-in. All attendance writes go through a single attendance service, which records the source of each change. Office staff currently phone parents manually. The enhancement reuses the attendance service as the trigger point and adds a notification subsystem.

Attendance service emits an event on every status change; no UI change for teachers.
Office phones parents manually each morning; no record kept.
Automatic email and in-app notifications with a full delivery log.
Parents can sign in and view basic student information.

Shows absence reason and response status; new office follow-up list.
Adds notification settings, cut-off times and template editor.
Reused for notifications with delivery-status webhooks.
Notify every linked parent when a student is marked Absent after the cut-off time.
Optionally notify parents when a student is marked Late (school setting).
Send a correction when a record changes to Present within the correction window.
Parents submit a reason and optional attachment from the notification link or portal.
Teachers and office see reasons; office sees unanswered absences after 11:00.
Parents choose email and/or in-app; at least one must stay on.
Admins set cut-off times, enable late notices and edit English/Khmer templates.
Log every send and delivery status; monthly report by class.
An Absent status that exists at or after the school cut-off time triggers one notification per linked parent per student per day (BR-01).
Late notifications are sent only when the school setting late_notify_enabled is true (BR-02).
Each notification is delivered through every channel the parent has enabled; in-app is always created as the record of the message (BR-03, BR-09).
If a status changes from Absent/Late to Present within 30 minutes of the first notification, exactly one correction message is sent; later changes are logged only (BR-04).
A parent can submit one reason per student per absence date; resubmission replaces the earlier reason and keeps a history (BR-05).
Reasons and response status appear on the teacher class list and the office follow-up list (BR-06, BR-07).
The follow-up list shows absences with no reason and no successful delivery, or no reason by 11:00 school time (BR-07).
Only administrators can change cut-off times, late settings and templates; template changes are versioned (BR-08).
Parents cannot disable all channels; the API rejects a preference update that would leave none enabled (BR-09).
Every send attempt and delivery-status update is stored in the notification log (BR-10).
Students without a linked parent are listed on the follow-up list as "No guardian contact" instead of failing silently.

Notification settings per school: cut-off time, late notifications on/off, follow-up time (default 11:00).

blocks.text: The enhancement adds a Notification module inside the existing SAMS backend. The attendance service publishes status-change events to an outbox table in the same transaction as the attendance write. A scheduled Notification Worker reads due events, applies the rules and sends messages through channel adapters. This keeps teacher attendance fast and makes notifications reliable even if email is slow.

  T["Teacher Web / QR"] --> API["SAMS API (Express)"]
  P["Parent Portal"] --> API
  O["Office / Admin UI"] --> API
  API --> AS["Attendance Service"]
  AS --> DB[("PostgreSQL")]
  AS --> OB[("Notification Outbox")]
  W["Notification Worker (every minute)"] --> OB
  W --> R["Rules Engine"]
  R --> DB
  W --> EM["Email Adapter"]
  W --> IA["In-app Adapter"]
  EM --> SG["SendGrid"]
  SG -- "delivery webhook" --> API
  IA --> DB
  API --> FS["File Storage (attachments)"]

items: A teacher marks attendance; the attendance service writes the record and an outbox event in one transaction.
The worker reads due events, loads guardians, preferences, settings and templates, and sends messages.
SendGrid reports delivered, bounced or dropped status back through the webhook into the notification log.
A parent opens the signed link, submits a reason, and the reason becomes visible to staff immediately.
At the follow-up time, the follow-up service combines attendance, log and reason data for the office.

blocks.text: The design adds tables to the existing PostgreSQL schema and reuses the existing students, classes, users and attendance tables. All new tables use UUID primary keys and timestamps in UTC.

erDiagram
  STUDENT ||--o{ ATTENDANCE : has
  STUDENT ||--o{ STUDENT_GUARDIAN : "linked to"
  USERS ||--o{ STUDENT_GUARDIAN : "is guardian"
  ATTENDANCE ||--o{ NOTIFICATION_OUTBOX : emits
  ATTENDANCE ||--o{ NOTIFICATION_LOG : "notified by"
  USERS ||--o{ NOTIFICATION_LOG : receives
  USERS ||--o{ NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCE : sets
  ATTENDANCE ||--o| ABSENCE_REASON : explained_by
  ABSENCE_REASON ||--o{ REASON_ATTACHMENT : has
  NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE ||--o{ NOTIFICATION_LOG : renders
  NOTIFICATION_LOG {
    uuid id PK
    uuid attendance_id FK
    uuid guardian_id FK
    string channel
    string status
  }
  ABSENCE_REASON {
    uuid id PK
    uuid attendance_id FK
    string reason_type
    string reason_text
  }

Add is_primary and receives_notifications flags; UNIQUE(student_id, guardian_id).
Pending attendance events with due_at and processed_at; index on (processed_at, due_at).
One row per message per channel per guardian; UNIQUE(attendance_id, guardian_id, event_type, channel).
One row per guardian: email_enabled, in_app_enabled, language; CHECK at least one channel on.
Versioned templates by school, event_type and language; only one active version.
Per school: cutoff_time, late_notify_enabled, followup_time, correction_window_min.
Current reason per attendance record; history kept in ABSENCE_REASON_HISTORY.
File metadata; files stored outside the database.
Office "contacted" actions with staff user, time and note.
QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED, BOUNCED, FAILED, READ

items: Write the attendance change and the outbox event in one database transaction so no event is lost.
The unique constraint on NOTIFICATION_LOG prevents duplicate notifications if the worker retries.
The worker selects outbox rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so two worker instances never process the same event.
Guardian deletion cascades to preferences; notification logs keep the guardian ID but personal contact data is not copied into the log.
Logs and reasons older than the academic year plus 90 days are deleted by a nightly job after monthly aggregates are stored.

blocks.text: All endpoints are added to the existing Express API, use the existing JWT authentication and role checks, and are documented in Swagger.

rows: Parent inbox, newest first; parent role required.
Marks an in-app message as read.
Read/update preferences; 422 if no channel enabled.
Student, date and status for the reason form; 410 if expired.
token or session, reason_type, reason_text, attachments
Creates or replaces the reason; returns saved reason.
Reasons and response status for a class; teacher/office role.
List or create a new template version; admin role.

items: Select outbox events where processed_at is null and due_at <= now, locking rows with SKIP LOCKED (batch of 200).
Load the current attendance status; if it no longer matches the event, mark the event processed and stop.
For ABSENT, require that the time is at or after the school cut-off; for LATE, require late_notify_enabled.
For PRESENT, send a CORRECTION only if an ABSENCE/LATE notification was sent within the correction window.
Load linked guardians with receives_notifications = true; if none, add the student to the follow-up list as "No guardian contact".
For each guardian and enabled channel, insert a QUEUED log row (skipping duplicates), render the template and send.
Update the log with SENT or FAILED; retry FAILED email up to 3 times with 1, 5 and 15 minute back-off.
Mark the outbox event processed.

blocks.text: The sequence diagrams show the order of calls for the two most important interactions and where authorization and validation happen.

sequenceDiagram
  participant T as Teacher
  participant API as SAMS API
  participant AS as Attendance Service
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant W as Notification Worker
  participant SG as SendGrid
  T->>API: POST attendance (Absent)

  AS->>DB: write attendance + outbox (one transaction)
  API-->>T: 200 OK
  W->>DB: lock due outbox events

  W->>DB: insert log (QUEUED)
  W->>SG: send email

  SG->>API: delivery webhook
  API->>DB: update log (DELIVERED)

blocks.text: **Design note:** the teacher request returns as soon as the attendance and outbox rows are written. Email sending happens in the worker, so a slow or failing email provider never blocks attendance taking.

blocks.text: **Design note:** the token identifies exactly one student and date and expires after 72 hours. It never grants access to other students or portal data.
Reporting supports the success measures in the BRD while keeping personal data to a minimum. Reports use monthly aggregates and are available only to administrators and the Head of Student Affairs.

items: All staff and parent endpoints use existing JWT authentication with role checks on the server.
Parents can only see notifications and students linked to their own account.
Reason tokens are HMAC-signed, scoped to one student and date, expire after 72 hours and are rate-limited.
The SendGrid webhook verifies the request signature before updating any record.
Attachments are type- and size-checked, stored outside the web root and served only through authorized download URLs.
Logs do not store message bodies or contact details; they reference the guardian by ID.
Retention follows Section 8.3 and the school data-protection policy.

The same build is promoted through the environments below. Secrets such as the SendGrid key and token signing key are stored in environment configuration, never in code or this document.
